chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from al-A'la ibn Razin and Abu Ayyub and Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him: What do you say about a woman who died leaving a husband, brothers from her mother, and brothers and sisters from her father?

He said: The husband gets half, which is three shares, and the brothers from the mother get one-third, which is two shares; male and female are equal in it. One share remains, which goes to the brothers and sisters from the father, for the male is like the share of two females, because the shares do not increase (due to scarcity), and the husband is not reduced from the half, nor are the brothers from the mother reduced from their one-third.
If there are more than that, they are partners in the one-third, and if there is only one, he gets one-sixth.

And indeed, what Allah meant in His saying, 'And if a man or woman leaves an heir (kalalah) and he or she has a brother or sister, for each one of them is one-sixth,' is that Allah meant by that the brothers and sisters from the mother specifically.
And if a man or woman leaves an heir (kalalah) and he or she has a brother or sister, for each one of them is one-sixth.

And He said in the end of Surah Al-Nisa: 'They ask you for a legal ruling. Say: Allah gives you a legal ruling regarding the kalalah: If a man dies leaving no child and he has a sister...' He means by that a sister from father and mother, and a sister from father.
They ask you for a legal ruling. Say: Allah gives you a legal ruling regarding the kalalah: If a man dies leaving no child and he has a sister.
Then for her is half of what he left, and he inherits her if she had no child.
'And if they are brothers, men and women, then for the male is the share of two females.' These are the ones who are increased and decreased.
And if they are brothers, men and women, then for the male is the share of two females.

He said: 'And if a woman left a husband, two sisters from her mother, and two sisters from her father, the husband gets half (three shares), and the two sisters from the mother get one-third (two shares), and the two sisters from the father get one share. And if there is only one, it is for her, because the two sisters from the father do not exceed what remains. So if there was a brother from the father, he would not exceed what remains.'

key_terms.اَلْكَلَالَةُ: Heir who leaves no direct descendants or ascendants
key_terms.لَا تَعُولُ: Do not increase (due to scarcity of shares)

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed when a deceased leaves a husband, maternal siblings, and paternal siblings?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the inheritance distribution for a woman leaving a husband, maternal siblings, and paternal siblings, establishing that the husband receives half, maternal siblings one-third (with equal shares for males and females), and paternal siblings the remainder. The Imam explicitly links the Quranic verse on 'Kalalah' (4:12) to maternal siblings and the concluding verses of Surah An-Nisa (4:176) to paternal siblings, demonstrating how Shia jurisprudence interprets these verses to resolve specific share allocations and the rule of 'la ta'ul' (shares do not increase due to scarcity).
